newsitem.title: USA: Brooke Group says settles class action suit.
newsitem.headline: Brooke Group says settles class action suit.

text.p: Brooke Group Ltd said on Thursday that, along with its Liggett Group tobacco subsidiary, it had reached a settlement in a class action suit in federal court in West Virginia that essentially stopped all class action and individual tobacco lawsuits against Liggett nationwide.
In return, Brooke and Liggett agreed to cooperate in prosecuting conspiracy claims against other tobacco companies, Brooke said in a statement.

In March, Brooke and Ligget announced they had reached a settlement in a state court in Alabama with class action tobacco plaintiffs that covered all smokers nationwide. Today's settlement is substantially based on the same terms as that agreement, Brooke said.

"We now have class action settlements in both federal and state court, which, upon approval, will give Brooke and Liggett near-universal protection," said Bennett LeBow, chief executive of Brooke Group.
The settlement agreement calls for Liggett to stop marketing its cigarettes to children and adolescents and to add strong warnings on cigarette packs regarding the addicitive nature of nicotine.
Ligget is also obligated to assist in lawsuits brought against other cigarette companies, including Philip Morris, by providing internal documents, testimony and witnesses.
